runs.text: 1. Earnings, not debt, drove the rise in leverage. Net debt moved from USD 1,275.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,271.6 million at June 30, 2026, while adjusted operating income over twelve months fell to USD 313.0 million from USD 411.9 million, taking net debt to adjusted operating income to 4.06x from 3.10x and total debt to adjusted operating income to 5.54x from 4.32x [CP-1 C3]. The fall came mainly from Domestic Operations, whose segment adjusted operating income was USD 61.0 million in Q2 2026 against USD 126.3 million in Q2 2025 as subscription, advertising and content licensing revenue all fell [CP-1 table; CP-1A operating model]. Management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue, so the denominator carries more risk than the numerator. 2. Cash interest cover is thinner. Adjusted operating income covered cash interest paid 2.07x in the twelve months to June 30, 2026 against 2.63x in FY2025 [CP-1 C4]. Run-rate contractual coupon on the notes outstanding at June 30, 2026 is USD 156.0 million, which on the same earnings gives 2.01x [CP-1 C8]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization with no add-backs, total debt is 12.66x earnings, but that basis includes a USD 97.8 million non-cash impairment and is shown only to expose the gap to the adjusted measure [CP-1 C7]. 3. Liquidity is cash only. The company repaid the remaining Term Loan A and terminated the USD 175.0 million revolver on May 12, 2026, leaving cash of USD 464.0 million at June 30, 2026, of which about USD 136.5 million is held by foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 liquidity rows]. The unused USD 125.0 million receivables sale program is not a committed facility. This replaces a position where cash of USD 502.4 million was backed by USD 175.0 million undrawn at December 31, 2025. 4. The maturity profile is long but ordered against unsecured holders. After the March 2026 exchange, USD 420.5 million of 4.25% unsecured senior and convertible notes mature in February 2029 ahead of USD 1,315.1 million of 10.50% secured notes in July 2032 [CP-1 C11; CP-1A transactions]. Management states that cash and operating cash flow will not repay all debt at maturity and that it depends on capital markets access. Whether the 2032 indenture constrains refinancing the earlier notes is Insufficient Information. 5. Cash flow remains positive after capital spending, but is weaker. Free cash flow was USD 108.1 million in six months 2026 against USD 189.9 million in six months 2025, and USD 190.5 million over twelve months [CP-1 C5]. Debt principal has fallen by USD 633.8 million since December 31, 2024 [CP-1A calculations], largely through discounted repurchases, a tender and Term Loan A repayments. 6. Control and capital allocation matter to creditors. The Dolan family group owns all Class B stock and about 79% of voting power outside director elections, and the company bought back USD 30.0 million of stock in six months 2026 under an indenture amendment that allows up to USD 50.0 million of equity repurchases, with USD 87 million of board authorization remaining at June 30, 2026 [CP-1A governance]. Restricted payment capacity beyond the summarised amendment is Insufficient Information. 7. Two dated events sit after the balance sheet or before an unreported outcome. The Netflix licence of July 30, 2026 brings USD 500 million of fees, with management expecting about USD 25 million of cash in 2026 and about USD 100 million a year in 2027 to 2030; and a damages claim above USD 200 million had a trial set for October 27, 2026 with no outcome supplied [CP-1 subsequent events; CP-1A credit translations]. Neither is in June 30, 2026 balances, and both are limited by documents not supplied.

runs.text: Strengths. First, the company has no debt maturing before February 2029 and its secured notes run to July 2032, after it exchanged USD 861.3 million of 2029 secured notes (tagged Documentary Fact; basis maturity rows and the 2026 transaction summary). Second, it generates cash: USD 190.5 million of free cash flow over twelve months to June 30, 2026 and cash of USD 464.0 million, with total debt principal USD 633.8 million lower than at December 31, 2024 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 C5 and CP-1A calculations). Third, it owns a large share of its scripted content and franchises, and has licensed the Walking Dead Universe to Netflix for USD 500 million of fees over five years; the licence terms are Management Language and the contract is not supplied (basis CP-1A operating model and subsequent events). Fourth, its documented behaviour towards debt has been supportive: it repurchased and tendered senior notes at discounts in 2025 and repaid its Term Loan A (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance table). Fifth, reporting quality is high, with an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting for FY2025 (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. First, earnings are falling: Q2 2026 revenue was USD 547.5 million against USD 600.0 million and operating income USD 15.9 million against USD 64.5 million, while operating cost lines rose (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 table). Second, leverage and cover have weakened to 5.54x total and 4.06x net on adjusted operating income, and 2.07x cash interest cover (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 C3 and C4; the adjusted measure adds back restructuring and share-based compensation). Third, there is no committed back-up facility, and the company states it depends on capital markets to refinance (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 liquidity rows and CP-1A refinancing translation). Fourth, the earlier maturity is the junior one: USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes fall due in February 2029 ahead of the secured notes (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, revenue is exposed to a few distributors and to advertising and subscriber declines that management expects to continue, and a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 with exposure not stated (Documentary Fact for the filing; Insufficient Information for the exposure). Sixth, controlled equity, USD 30.0 million of buybacks and USD 87 million of authorization remaining while earnings fall (Documentary Fact; the creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). Seventh, the unresolved damages claim above USD 200 million against cash of USD 464.0 million (Documentary Fact; the outcome is Insufficient Information). Eighth, ranking and collateral for the 2032 notes cannot be settled because the filing describes the guarantees as unsecured while the notes are secured by a first-priority lien (Insufficient Information; no recovery conclusion is drawn).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The 2026 transaction set is a refinancing and simplification, not a cash raise. On February 23, 2026 the company launched an exchange offer for any and all of its $875 million of 10.25% Senior Secured Notes due January 2029 into additional 10.50% Senior Secured Notes due July 2032, which form part of the same series as the $400.0 million of 2032 notes issued in July 2025 (10-Q Q2-26 page:17-18). Holders tendering by March 6, 2026 received $1,065 of 2032 notes per $1,000 and later tenders $1,015; early settlement on March 13, 2026 issued about $884 million of notes against about $830.6 million tendered, and final settlement on March 25, 2026 issued about $31.1 million against about $30.7 million (page:18). The remaining 2029 notes of about $13.7 million were redeemed on April 6, 2026 at 105.125% of principal, with a $0.7 million charge (page:19). The 2032 notes outstanding are 1,315,098 (page:16). The incremental principal of $53.8 million was accounted for as a debt modification and recorded as a debt discount, and third-party exchange fees of $16.7 million were expensed in Miscellaneous, net (page:18). These are Documentary Facts. Status: completed.

In parallel, on February 23, 2026 the company received requisite consents to amend the indenture for the 2032 notes: to permit buybacks of equity interests up to an aggregate of $50.0 million, to limit transfers of certain trademarks to unrestricted subsidiaries to non-exclusive licences, and to restrict investments in unrestricted subsidiaries under the Permitted Investments definition to specified clauses; a $2.0 million consent fee was paid and capitalized (page:17). Status: effective. The legal terms themselves (definitions, baskets, ratio tests) are not supplied.

On May 12, 2026 the company repaid the $80.0 million remaining Term Loan A under the Credit Agreement and terminated the revolving credit facility, recording a $3.1 million charge (page:17; Rel Jul page:4). Status: completed. This ended the maintenance covenants of the Credit Agreement (CP-1 Gaps); no replacement committed facility is described.

The prior-year steps explain today's structure. In July 2025 the company issued $400.0 million of 10.50% secured notes due 2032 for net proceeds of $394.5 million, which with cash funded a tender of $600.0 million of 4.25% senior notes at a discount of $111.0 million and the prepayment of the remaining $70.0 million of the non-extended Term Loan A; during 2025 it also repurchased $108.3 million of senior notes in the open market at discounts of $28.2 million (10-K page:110). On October 29, 2025 Amendment No. 5 to the Credit Agreement extended $111.8 million of revolver commitments to the earlier of October 29, 2030 or 90 days before certain capital markets maturities, lowered the minimum interest coverage ratio to 1.50:1.00 and retired $165.7 million of term loans held by consenting lenders (10-K page:110-111, 169). On November 26, 2025 the company bought the remaining 17% of RLJ Entertainment for $75.0 million cash, and on November 1, 2024 the remaining 50.1% of BBC America for $42.0 million, together with a new $40.0 million program license agreement with BBC Studios (10-K page:190-191).

Use of proceeds and liquidity effect: none of the 2026 steps raised cash. Cash outflows were $82.9 million on the Term Loan A and $14.4 million on the 2029 notes redemption in six months 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:5), with debt principal falling to 1,735,554 and committed liquidity to nil at June 30, 2026 (CP-1 chart rows). Sponsor: none. Dividend recapitalisation: none documented; the cash flow statements show no dividend payments to stockholders in FY2025 or six months 2026 (10-K page:136; 10-Q Q2-26 page:5-6).

Analyst Interpretation: the exchange and the April 2026 redemption retired the whole 875,000 January 2029 secured maturity (about 861.3 million exchanged and about 13.7 million redeemed), extended secured debt to July 2032, and left the 4.25% unsecured senior and convertible notes of 420,456 as the next maturity in February 2029, ahead of the secured 2032 notes (CP-1 C11). The coupon on the exchanged debt rose from 10.25% to 10.50% and the principal exchanged rose by the early-tender and exchange premium. Whether the 2032 indenture restricts the company's ability to refinance the 2029 unsecured notes ahead of the secured notes is Insufficient Information, because the indenture is not supplied.

Subsequent event after June 30, 2026 and before the cutoff: the Netflix licence of July 30, 2026 (co-exclusive global streaming rights to The Walking Dead Universe; $500 million fee; expected present-value revenue about $445 million; expected recognition of $200 million to $225 million in each of 2026 and 2027) and an accelerated share repurchase of $30 million with Citibank entered on May 8, 2026 with final settlement expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 (Rel Jul page:4). These are Management Language and are not folded into June 30, 2026 balances.

Perimeter: consolidated; the debt note describes the Credit Agreement borrowers as certain subsidiaries with restricted subsidiaries as guarantors (page:170-171), so issuer, borrower and guarantor roles differ by instrument. Debt note (page:167) lists the Term Loan A Facility, the 10.25% Senior Secured Notes due January 2029, the 4.25% Senior Notes due February 2029, the 4.25% Convertible Senior Notes due February 2029 and the 10.50% Senior Secured Notes due July 2032. Covenant text (page:110-111) gives the credit-facility tests and the year-end reported ratios. Collateral for the 2032 notes is described at page:171 ("secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all of" the issuer's and the guarantors' assets and property).

These management measures do not override the filings. The credit-agreement ratios are printed only in the December 2025 and March 2026 releases and the filings up to the first quarter of 2026.

fields.value: The financial base is a consolidated, USD, filed-statement base from the 10-K and the June 30, 2026 10-Q, with company releases used only as attributed support. On the company's adjusted operating income (AOI, a non-GAAP measure that adds back share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, restructuring, impairment and cloud computing amortization and adds the proportionate AOI of majority-owned equity investees) the twelve months to June 30, 2026 produced 313,045 against 411,874 for FY2025. Total debt principal fell from 1,778,251 to 1,735,554 and cash from 502,379 to 463,996, so net debt was 1,275,872 and then 1,271,558. The result is gross debt to AOI of 5.54x and net debt to AOI of 4.06x at June 30, 2026, against 4.32x and 3.10x at FY2025, with AOI to cash interest paid of 2.07x against 2.63x. These ratios use the AOI definition and are not the credit-agreement ratios, which were last reported at March 31, 2026 (net leverage 5.11x against a 5.75x maximum that applied through March 31, 2026 and steps down to 5.50x after; interest coverage 1.85x against a 1.50x minimum) and ended with the facility on May 12, 2026. Using reported operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with no add-backs, the same debt gives much higher multiples because the twelve-month windows include a non-cash impairment charge of 97,784 recorded in Q4 2025; both bases are shown in the calculations and the chart rows use the AOI basis. The base supports the report's leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity charts for three period ends, with the limits listed under Gaps.

fields.value: - **AOI.** Defined in the segment note as operating income before depreciation and amortization, cloud computing amortization, share-based compensation, impairment and other charges, restructuring and other related charges, and including the proportionate share of adjusted operating income of majority-owned equity method investees (10-Q Q2-26 page:28). It is a segment measure and a non-GAAP total; it is not EBITDA. Three consequences: it excludes restructuring cash costs (cash paid for restructuring initiatives was 19,729 in 6M 2026 against 7,920 in 6M 2025, Rel Jul page:11), it adds back equity-classified and some other share-based compensation, and it adds investee AOI that is not consolidated cash flow (6,762 in 6M 2026).

fields.value: - **EBITDA on a reported basis.** Operating income plus depreciation and amortization, with no add-backs. The twelve-month windows to March 31 and June 30, 2026 include the Q4 2025 non-cash impairment and other charges of 97,784 (10-K page:134; Q4 2025 timing per 10-Q Q2-26 page:16), so this basis understates run-rate earnings; it is shown in C7 for transparency, not charted.

The company's own leverage ratio (3.1x at FY2025, 3.4x at March 31, 2026, 4.1x at June 30, 2026) divides net debt and finance leases by AOI (Rel Feb page:11, Rel May page:9, Rel Jul page:11); the difference from C3 is the finance lease liability (13,882 at June 30, 2026, Rel Jul page:11).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC Global Media is a holding company that owns and operates linear cable networks (AMC, We TV, BBC America, IFC, SundanceTV), a portfolio of subscription streaming services (AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder, Sundance Now, ALLBLK, HIDIVE, All Reality), a studio that owns much of its scripted content and a film distribution arm, plus an international channels business. Revenue comes from per-subscriber affiliate fees and streaming subscriptions, advertising sold on ratings guarantees, and content licensing that is lumpy by delivery timing. The business is controlled by the Dolan family group through a dual-class structure, not by a financial sponsor, so the sponsor-behaviour lens is applied to documented issuer actions only. The credit-relevant history is a sequence of liability-management steps: repurchases and a tender of the 4.25% senior notes and a new 10.50% secured issue in 2025, purchase of the remaining minority interests in BBC America and RLJ Entertainment in 2024 and 2025, an exchange of the 10.25% secured notes into the 10.50% notes in March 2026, an indenture consent that widened the buyback covenant, and in May 2026 the repayment of the Term Loan A and termination of the revolver. The creditor view is that the maturity profile has been pushed out while earnings and liquidity buffers have narrowed (CP-1 C3), that the remaining protections sit in indentures this source set does not contain, and that a pending damages claim and a streaming licence with Netflix are the main identified swing factors after June 30, 2026. The evidence is strong for facts stated in the filings and weak where it depends on management expectations or on documents not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 transaction set is a refinancing and simplification, not a cash raise. On February 23, 2026 the company launched an exchange offer for any and all of its $875 million of 10.25% Senior Secured Notes due January 2029 into additional 10.50% Senior Secured Notes due July 2032, which form part of the same series as the $400.0 million of 2032 notes issued in July 2025 (10-Q Q2-26 page:17-18). Holders tendering by March 6, 2026 received $1,065 of 2032 notes per $1,000 and later tenders $1,015; early settlement on March 13, 2026 issued about $884 million of notes against about $830.6 million tendered, and final settlement on March 25, 2026 issued about $31.1 million against about $30.7 million (page:18). The remaining 2029 notes of about $13.7 million were redeemed on April 6, 2026 at 105.125% of principal, with a $0.7 million charge (page:19). The 2032 notes outstanding are 1,315,098 (page:16). The incremental principal of $53.8 million was accounted for as a debt modification and recorded as a debt discount, and third-party exchange fees of $16.7 million were expensed in Miscellaneous, net (page:18). These are Documentary Facts. Status: completed.

fields.value: The prior-year steps explain today's structure. In July 2025 the company issued $400.0 million of 10.50% secured notes due 2032 for net proceeds of $394.5 million, which with cash funded a tender of $600.0 million of 4.25% senior notes at a discount of $111.0 million and the prepayment of the remaining $70.0 million of the non-extended Term Loan A; during 2025 it also repurchased $108.3 million of senior notes in the open market at discounts of $28.2 million (10-K page:110). On October 29, 2025 Amendment No. 5 to the Credit Agreement extended $111.8 million of revolver commitments to the earlier of October 29, 2030 or 90 days before certain capital markets maturities, lowered the minimum interest coverage ratio to 1.50:1.00 and retired $165.7 million of term loans held by consenting lenders (10-K page:110-111, 169). On November 26, 2025 the company bought the remaining 17% of RLJ Entertainment for $75.0 million cash, and on November 1, 2024 the remaining 50.1% of BBC America for $42.0 million, together with a new $40.0 million program license agreement with BBC Studios (10-K page:190-191).

Sponsor: none. Dividend recapitalisation: none documented; the cash flow statements show no dividend payments to stockholders in FY2025 or six months 2026 (10-K page:136; 10-Q Q2-26 page:5-6).

The coupon on the exchanged debt rose from 10.25% to 10.50% and the principal exchanged rose by the early-tender and exchange premium. Whether the 2032 indenture restricts the company's ability to refinance the 2029 unsecured notes ahead of the secured notes is Insufficient Information, because the indenture is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. **Revenue durability.** Evidence: Domestic subscription revenue is declining on basic subscriber losses, advertising is lower on ratings and pricing, and content licensing fell by 32.4% in Q2 2026 on delivery timing (10-Q Q2-26 page:42-44); management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue. Risk mechanic: technical and operating and selling, general and administrative costs rose while revenue fell (10-Q Q2-26 page:3), so the revenue loss fell through to operating income (page:47). Credit implication: debt service depends on streaming growth, price increases and licensing, which are less predictable; the Netflix licence adds expected cash of about $25 million in 2026 and about $100 million a year in 2027 to 2030 but is Management Language and the contract is not supplied. Countering item: none logged as a conflict.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. **Margin and cash-flow risk.** Evidence: Q2 2026 operating income fell from 64,469 to 15,854 on a revenue decrease of 52.5 million (10-Q Q2-26 page:47); twelve-month AOI of 313,045 against cash interest paid of 151,153 gives 2.07x cover (CP-1 C4). Mechanic: fixed programming and marketing cost base with falling revenue compresses cover; the run-rate contractual coupon on notes outstanding is 155,955 (CP-1 C8). Implication: limited tolerance for further earnings decline before leverage and cover weaken; the net debt to AOI ratio was 4.06x at June 30, 2026 (CP-1 C3).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. **Concentration.** Evidence: few distributors hold a concentration of subscribers; two customers were 13% and 10% of receivables at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:146-147); a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 and sought authority to pay prepetition ordinary-course claims for which the company is named as a vendor (10-Q Q2-26 page:57). Mechanic: renewal repricing and counterparty failure hit revenue and receivables together. Implication: receivables of 547,187 at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:2) are exposed to counterparty events; exposure to the filing customer is Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. **Sponsor and control alignment.** Evidence: family control and ownership of all Class B stock (10-K page:72-73); the 2032 indenture was amended to allow buybacks up to $50.0 million, and 30,000 of treasury stock was bought in six months 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:6, 17), with $87 million of authorization remaining (Rel Jul page:4). Mechanic: controlled equity can direct cash to buybacks within indenture capacity at the expense of debt reduction or liquidity. Implication: monitoring item for restricted payment capacity; the gap between the $87 million board authorization and the $50.0 million indenture basket as summarised is not resolved by the sources because other baskets may apply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. **Refinancing.** Evidence: no debt due before February 2029 when 420,456 of unsecured 4.25% notes mature, and 1,315,098 of secured notes in July 2032; management states cash flow and cash will not repay all maturities and the company depends on capital markets access (10-Q Q2-26 page:55-56). Mechanic: the unsecured notes mature ahead of the secured notes; refinancing the earlier maturity depends on earnings stabilising. Implication: refinancing risk is deferred, not removed; the revolving facility's absence removes a bridge.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. **Key uncertainty: litigation.** Evidence: plaintiffs claim damages in excess of $200 million in the MFN Litigation; summary judgment motion was filed; trial rescheduled to October 27, 2026; the company believes the claims are without merit and no determination of outcome can be made (10-Q Q2-26 page:24-25). Mechanic: an adverse result would be a cash claim against liquidity of cash 463,996 with no revolver. Implication: unquantified event risk dated before the as-of date with no outcome supplied; no loss estimate is recorded in the pages read.

fields.value: No document conflict on a fact was found in the pages read. One unresolved wording tension is logged, not reconciled: the 10-K says the notes are guaranteed by domestic restricted subsidiaries "on an unsecured basis" (10-K page:112; repeated in 10-Q Q2-26 page:60), while the 2032 secured notes are described as secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all assets (10-K page:171). Effect: ranking and collateral coverage for the 2032 notes cannot be settled from the filings; any recovery mechanic that depends on it is withheld. A second, minor change over time is not a conflict: the MFN trial date moved from March 26, 2026 to April 21, 2026 (10-K page:188) and then to October 27, 2026 (10-Q Q2-26 page:24).

fields.value: AMC Global Media Inc. credit snapshot as of 2026-11-05 (pathway credit_snapshot; current period Q2 2026, prior period FY2025; reporting currency USD). This module synthesises the fundamental credit view from the financial base and the business and transaction handoffs, and reads no source text directly. It gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CP-2 uses upstream registers only. The seven issuer sources below were the evidence behind the handoffs; none was re-read for this module.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: AMC Global Media has a weakening but refinanced credit profile: it faces no debt maturity until February 2029, but its earnings are falling and its liquidity is now cash alone. The strongest support is cash generation, with USD 190.5 million of free cash flow in the twelve months to June 30, 2026 and cash of USD 464.0 million. The weakest point is earnings: adjusted operating income fell to USD 313.0 million from USD 411.9 million in FY2025, which lifted net debt to adjusted operating income to 4.06x from 3.10x while net debt was flat at USD 1,271.6 million, and the revolving credit facility no longer exists. The outcome depends on whether streaming growth and the Netflix licence cash offset linear decline before USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes fall due in February 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Assessment: weakening, refinanced credit; category Analyst Interpretation; confidence Medium. The basis is the leverage, cover and liquidity figures [CP-1 C3, C4, C5, C11] and the business rows on revenue, control and transactions [CP-1A]. Confidence is below High because the business module judged this module ready only with limitations and listed unsupplied indentures as a high-severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thesis: AMC Global Media has traded near-term maturity risk for a higher-cost, longer secured structure at the point its earnings are declining, so the credit now rests on stabilising earnings and cash generation rather than on committed back-up liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Earnings, not debt, drove the rise in leverage. Net debt moved from USD 1,275.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 1,271.6 million at June 30, 2026, while adjusted operating income over twelve months fell to USD 313.0 million from USD 411.9 million, taking net debt to adjusted operating income to 4.06x from 3.10x and total debt to adjusted operating income to 5.54x from 4.32x [CP-1 C3]. The fall came mainly from Domestic Operations, whose segment adjusted operating income was USD 61.0 million in Q2 2026 against USD 126.3 million in Q2 2025 as subscription, advertising and content licensing revenue all fell [CP-1 table; CP-1A operating model]. Management expects linear subscriber and advertising declines to continue, so the denominator carries more risk than the numerator.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Cash interest cover is thinner. Adjusted operating income covered cash interest paid 2.07x in the twelve months to June 30, 2026 against 2.63x in FY2025 [CP-1 C4]. Run-rate contractual coupon on the notes outstanding at June 30, 2026 is USD 156.0 million, which on the same earnings gives 2.01x [CP-1 C8]. On operating income plus depreciation and amortization with no add-backs, total debt is 12.66x earnings, but that basis includes a USD 97.8 million non-cash impairment and is shown only to expose the gap to the adjusted measure [CP-1 C7].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Liquidity is cash only. The company repaid the remaining Term Loan A and terminated the USD 175.0 million revolver on May 12, 2026, leaving cash of USD 464.0 million at June 30, 2026, of which about USD 136.5 million is held by foreign subsidiaries [CP-1 liquidity rows]. The unused USD 125.0 million receivables sale program is not a committed facility. This replaces a position where cash of USD 502.4 million was backed by USD 175.0 million undrawn at December 31, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. The maturity profile is long but ordered against unsecured holders. After the March 2026 exchange, USD 420.5 million of 4.25% unsecured senior and convertible notes mature in February 2029 ahead of USD 1,315.1 million of 10.50% secured notes in July 2032 [CP-1 C11; CP-1A transactions]. Management states that cash and operating cash flow will not repay all debt at maturity and that it depends on capital markets access. Whether the 2032 indenture constrains refinancing the earlier notes is Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Cash flow remains positive after capital spending, but is weaker. Free cash flow was USD 108.1 million in six months 2026 against USD 189.9 million in six months 2025, and USD 190.5 million over twelve months [CP-1 C5]. Debt principal has fallen by USD 633.8 million since December 31, 2024 [CP-1A calculations], largely through discounted repurchases, a tender and Term Loan A repayments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Control and capital allocation matter to creditors. The Dolan family group owns all Class B stock and about 79% of voting power outside director elections, and the company bought back USD 30.0 million of stock in six months 2026 under an indenture amendment that allows up to USD 50.0 million of equity repurchases, with USD 87 million of board authorization remaining at June 30, 2026 [CP-1A governance]. Restricted payment capacity beyond the summarised amendment is Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Two dated events sit after the balance sheet or before an unreported outcome. The Netflix licence of July 30, 2026 brings USD 500 million of fees, with management expecting about USD 25 million of cash in 2026 and about USD 100 million a year in 2027 to 2030; and a damages claim above USD 200 million had a trial set for October 27, 2026 with no outcome supplied [CP-1 subsequent events; CP-1A credit translations]. Neither is in June 30, 2026 balances, and both are limited by documents not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. First, the company has no debt maturing before February 2029 and its secured notes run to July 2032, after it exchanged USD 861.3 million of 2029 secured notes (tagged Documentary Fact; basis maturity rows and the 2026 transaction summary). Second, it generates cash: USD 190.5 million of free cash flow over twelve months to June 30, 2026 and cash of USD 464.0 million, with total debt principal USD 633.8 million lower than at December 31, 2024 (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 C5 and CP-1A calculations). Third, it owns a large share of its scripted content and franchises, and has licensed the Walking Dead Universe to Netflix for USD 500 million of fees over five years; the licence terms are Management Language and the contract is not supplied (basis CP-1A operating model and subsequent events). Fourth, its documented behaviour towards debt has been supportive: it repurchased and tendered senior notes at discounts in 2025 and repaid its Term Loan A (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1A governance table). Fifth, reporting quality is high, with an unqualified audit opinion and effective internal control over financial reporting for FY2025 (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. First, earnings are falling: Q2 2026 revenue was USD 547.5 million against USD 600.0 million and operating income USD 15.9 million against USD 64.5 million, while operating cost lines rose (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 table). Second, leverage and cover have weakened to 5.54x total and 4.06x net on adjusted operating income, and 2.07x cash interest cover (Analyst Interpretation of CP-1 C3 and C4; the adjusted measure adds back restructuring and share-based compensation). Third, there is no committed back-up facility, and the company states it depends on capital markets to refinance (Documentary Fact; basis CP-1 liquidity rows and CP-1A refinancing translation). Fourth, the earlier maturity is the junior one: USD 420.5 million of unsecured notes fall due in February 2029 ahead of the secured notes (Analyst Interpretation). Fifth, revenue is exposed to a few distributors and to advertising and subscriber declines that management expects to continue, and a customer filed for Chapter 11 on June 30, 2026 with exposure not stated (Documentary Fact for the filing; Insufficient Information for the exposure). Sixth, controlled equity, USD 30.0 million of buybacks and USD 87 million of authorization remaining while earnings fall (Documentary Fact; the creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). Seventh, the unresolved damages claim above USD 200 million against cash of USD 464.0 million (Documentary Fact; the outcome is Insufficient Information). Eighth, ranking and collateral for the 2032 notes cannot be settled because the filing describes the guarantees as unsecured while the notes are secured by a first-priority lien (Insufficient Information; no recovery conclusion is drawn).
